The cold start service is called to initialize everything from scratch, reset the paths, startup, and order all vehicles to $Nan initial station to get the system going.  At step 5, the cold start service is dormant and doesn$'t do anything (so we return from the routine)

At Step 10 call init_constants and init_stations to get everything initialized.$NClear the timeout counts for postition / path commands.$NSet the HLC link status initially down and prev heartbeat to current one so hlc_link_monitor can determine initially if we are talking to the HLC upon first hlc_link_monitor_timer expiry.$NRun for loop routine to clear the active flag for each entry in the pos_order tag.  Logic will later select which entries in that array to have the HLC pay attention to.$NThis routine will start the system and discover all vehicles on the track.$NSet the path cmd and position order msg service routine steps to 10 so they are available for work.$NThen move on to step 20

Clear the active flag for all 8 entries in the position_order MSG source area$NLogic outside here chooses which entries the HLC should pay attention to in$Nthe MSG content by setting active_flag for a particular element.
Clear all records in the vehicle manager storage array$NThis will allow the vehicle manager array to be repopulated only with detected and ordered vehicle$NPrevents stale data
Wait for all NCs to be in the operational state before resetting.

When at step 20 and HLC link is up and path cmd msg service is available for work, format a reset command in path_cmd tag.$NSet path_id to zero for all paths, reset command, active flag so HLC acts on this single path cmd entry.$Nuse next_command_count routine to get a new command count and store in cold_start_service.  Store command count in path_cmd$NSet the msg_service_path_cmd_step to 20 to let the msg service do the msg for us.$NSet up the cold start service timer for 10 seconds so we can wait for path command completion or timeout so we can retry.$NGo to next step 30$N
Initialize variables for step 30$Nrestart cold start routine if process times out

At step 30, set the number of paths done with our command to 0$NRun a loop to check if each path has finished reset by seeing if the last accepted command for all paths has completed.$Nif it has, the logic increments paths_done_with_cmd to the number of paths that have completed reset.$NWhen all paths have completed reset, it advances to the next step

Reset is done, when path_cmd msg service is ready at step 10, format a startup command the same way we formatted the reset command above and tell msg service to kick the command and set a timeout again.$N
Initialize variables for step 60$Nrestart cold start routine if process times out

At step 60, set the number of paths done with our command to 0$NRun a loop to check if each path has finished startup by seeing if the last accepted command for all paths has completed.$Nif it has, the logic increments paths_done_with_cmd to the number of paths that have completed reset.$NWhen all paths have completed startup, it advances to the next step

When startup is done, set our timer for 1 second to give the HLC a chance to push the latest vehicle status for all located$Nvehicles into the MMI_vehicle_status array so we can go through there and determine how many vehicles we have located.
When our 1 second wait after startup is complete at step 80, move on to step 90

Go through each vehicle record in MMI_vehicle_status and determine valid vehicles we have found (path ID field in MMI_vehicle_status record is non-zero) and$Nschedule with the vehicle manager to order each discovered vehicle to an initial station to get things going.  Set the step to 5, cold start complete.$N
Pet the cold start service timer every scan

This routine watches the MMI_Heartbeat tag from the HLC and sets hlc_link_status when it is known the HLC is talking to us (heartbeat is changing)$Nand clears hlc_link_status when it is known the HLC is not talking to us (no heartbeat change).$N$NPet the hlc_link_monitor_timer tag every scan

When link monitor timer is done (3 seconds), check if heartbeat changed -- if so and link is considered down, latch it to up.$NIf heartbeat didn$'t change and the link is considered up, latch it down.$NCopy the current heartbeat to previous for the next check and reset the timer for the next go-around.

Store command count in path_cmd$NSet the msg_service_path_cmd_step to 20 to let the msg service do the msg for us.$NSet up the cold start service timer for 10 seconds so we can wait for path command completion or timeout so we can retry.$NGo to next step 30$N

The station_mgr routine is called off a FOR loop in the main routine to go through each stations_array entry and check$Nif the vehicle_mgr detected any vehicle arriving at said station (by setting active_vehicle_id field non-zero) and act on the vehicle$'s arrival:$Neither dwell for the dwell period, or go straight to the depart state to assign the vehicle$'s vehicle_mgr_array entry dest_station_id field to$Na new station to head to.$N$NWhen in the STATION_STATE_IDLE, and the hold_flag isn$'t set, if this station entry$'s active_vehicle_id goes non-zero, a vehicle$Narrived here.  Ifwe have a non-zero dwell period, schedule the dwell and go to STATION_STATE_DWELL$Notherwise go to the STATION_STATE_DEPART state to get the vehicle on to the next_station_id field.$N$NThe station_mgr and vehicle_mgr work hand-in-hand to move vehicles from station to station stored here in$NPLC memory only which can be more convenient than defining all of your stations with the HLC XML file.$NThis is a technique used at MMI we pass on as a example for convenience to those looking for example logic$Nto do a station to station based setup.
When we$'re in the STATION_STATE_DWELL, pet the dwell timer, check if it$'s done, and when done go to STATION_STATE_DEPART

When in STATION_STATE_DEPART, save a copy of the vehicle_id that arrived here in active_vehicle_id and set the dest_station_id of the vehicle_mgr_array entry for$Nthe vehicle sitting here to our next_station_id field so the vehicle will take off (taken care of by vehicle_mgr).$NIf clear_loaded_flag is set, clear the loaded_flag field for this vehicle in vehicle_mgr_array entry$NIf set_loaded_flag is set for this station, set the loaded_flag for this vehicle in vehicle_mgr_array_entry.$NFinally, go back to STATION_STATE_IDLE to wait for the vehicle_mgr to populate us with a new active_vehicle_id (it will go non-zero).$N

The vehicle_mgr routine is called of a FOR loop in the main_routine to go through each vehicle_mgr_array entry and see if it$'s IDLE and picked up$Nan order to a station -- if so the order will be scheduled with the msg service.$N$NFor vehicles on their way in WAIT_FOR_ARRIVAL state, this routine checks if the vehicle$'s order is complete and sets it to arrived in$Nthe stations_array for the station_mgr to do it$'s work upon a vehicle arrival.$N$N$NWhen this vehicle_mgr_array entry is IDLE and it picked up a dest_station_id (non-zero), and the msg_service is available$Nto place an order for us, go to the PLACE_ORDER state to format and schdule the order with the msg_service.

When we hit the PLACE_ORDER state, save the arrived_station_id field and zero it out in this vehicle_mgr_array entry -- this vehicle is going to depart!$NSave the dest_station_id field in the vehicle_mgr_array record in dest_station_id.$NSet first order entry in position_order array to the path the dest_station_id is on.$NSet the position in position_order entry to the position along the path we need to go to.$N$NWhen this vehicle wasn$'t sitting at a station (arrived_station_id is zero -- which happens upon initial order at cold start), use fixed values to place the initial order.$NWhen the vehicle is sitting at a station, use this station$'s velocity, accel, direction (which go with the next station vehicle is heading to).$N$NGet a new order number, use a Bit field distribute instruction to move the binary form of the PID value into the correct section og the flags and direction byte, set active_flag in position_order array entry, and schedule the order$Nwith the msg_service and go to the WAIT_FOR_ARRIVAL state.  When there are multiple vehicles that need to get ordered,$Nthis routine round-robins through the vehicle list scheduling orders with the msg_service who turns around getting the orders off $Nquickly, so multiple vehicles will simply get ordered in rapid succession off the one MSG instruction used in the MSG service.$N

When in the WAIT_FOR_ARRIVAL state, check if the last order accepted for this vehicle is complete,  store the station vehicle is heading to$N in dest_station_id and check the station vehicle is heading to is free (station$'s active_vehicle_id field is zero), if so the vehicle arrived:$NStore the vehicle ID (which is index i) in the station$'s active_vehicle_id field so the station_mgr will know a vehicle of ID i has arrived at the station it was heading to!$NSet the arrived_station_id field of the vehicle_mgr record to the station id for convenience -- this vehicle is now at the station it was heading to.$N$NSet the vehicle_mgr station to IDLE to wait for the station_mgr to set our dest_station_id field to non-zero when it$'s time for us to head$Nto another station.$N
